scenario.name: Microsoft MSRC & Dirk-jan Mollema DFIR — Entra ID Primary Refresh Token (PRT) & Rogue Device Registration Forensics
scenario.overview: Imagine a cloud office park that issues long-lived resident smartcards to company-owned laptops so workers stay signed in seamlessly across every building. Using a hijacked login token, an intruder walks up to the laptop-enrollment desk, registers a completely fake phantom laptop into the corporate directory, and collects a genuine long-lived smartcard that lets them mint fresh building passes quietly even from off-site machines. In this scenario (T1528, Microsoft MSRC & Dirk-jan Mollema DFIR, Entra ID Primary Refresh Token , PRT & Rogue Device Registration Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: token Acquisition for Device Registration, then rogue Device Registration in Entra ID, then primary Refresh Token Sign-In. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Token Acquisition for Device Registration, then Rogue Device Registration in Entra ID, then Primary Refresh Token Sign-In, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on Azure AD Event 100 correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 2: Rogue Device Registration in Entra ID Directory Audit Logs (Operation="Register device")
stages.subtitle: Persistence (T1098.005 - Account Manipulation: Device Registration)
stages.description: Presenting that enrollment pass alongside a freshly generated machine key pair, the intruder registers a phantom computer directly into the corporate directory, receiving a genuine company device certificate while the directory audit ledger stamps a brand-new registration line. The actor submits a locally generated RSA transport key and device certificate CSR to the DRS endpoint. Entra ID Audit Logs record Category="Device", ActivityDisplayName="Register device" (and "Add registered users to device" / "Add registered owner to device"), creating a persistent DeviceId in the tenant (logged in Network Event 200 with LogCategory=Entra ID AuditLogs , Device Registration Service, OperationName=Register device, RegisteredDeviceName=WIN-DESKTOP-991A , DeviceId d4819c02-..., InitiatingUser=admin_cloud@corp.com so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). stages.title: Stage 3: Primary Refresh Token (PRT) Sign-In & Persistent Session Key Forensics (IncomingTokenType=primaryRefreshToken)
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1550.001 - Primary Refresh Token Persistence Across Password Reset)
stages.description: Using the newly issued phantom device certificate, the intruder requests a long-lived Primary Resident Smartcard and its matching cryptographic session key, allowing them to stamp fresh multi-factor-satisfied cloud passes persistently until defenders delete the rogue device. Using the registered device certificate and software session key, the actor requests a Primary Refresh Token (PRT) valid for 14 days (renewable for 90 days) that persists across user password changes until the device object itself is disabled or deleted in Entra ID. Subsequent sign-ins show IncomingTokenType="primaryRefreshToken" and DeviceDetail.deviceId="d4819c02-..." (logged in Network Event 200 with LogCategory=Entra ID SignInLogs, IncomingTokenType=primaryRefreshToken , PRT, DeviceId=d4819c02-5511-4a90-8111-223344556677, IrRemediation=Disable/delete rogue DeviceId + Revoke-MgUserSignInSession so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Next, the follow-up artifact Remediation: Set-MgDevice -DeviceId d4819c02-... -AccountEnabled:$false; Revoke-MgUserSignInSession runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Remediation: Set-MgDevice -DeviceId d4819c02-... -AccountEnabled:$false; Revoke-MgUserSignIn so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1550.001 during "Primary Refresh Token , PRT Sign-In & Persistent Session Key Forensics , IncomingTokenType=primaryRefreshToken" , Using the registered device certificate and software session key, the actor requests a Primary Refresh Token , PRT valid for 14 days , renewable for 90 days that persists across user password changes until the device object itself is disabled or deleted in Entra ID while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ Entra SignInLogs: IncomingTokenType=primaryRefreshToken from DeviceId d4819c02-... / ⇠#3 RESP 200) from Node ③ (#3 Entra ID DRS Service) to Node ④ (#4 Registered Device Object), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 PRT Sign-In (IncomingToken PRT)).

steps.plainTitle: Primary Refresh Token (PRT) Sign-In & Persistent Session Key Forensics (IncomingTokenType=primaryRefreshToken)
steps.storyAnalogy: Using the newly issued phantom device certificate, the intruder requests a long-lived Primary Resident Smartcard and its matching cryptographic session key, allowing them to stamp fresh multi-factor-satisfied cloud passes persistently until defenders delete the rogue device.
steps.simpleExplanation: Using the registered device certificate and software session key, the actor requests a Primary Refresh Token (PRT) valid for 14 days (renewable for 90 days) that persists across user password changes until the device object itself is disabled or deleted in Entra ID. Subsequent sign-ins show IncomingTokenType="primaryRefreshToken" and DeviceDetail.deviceId="d4819c02-..." (logged in Network Event 200 with LogCategory=Entra ID SignInLogs, IncomingTokenType=primaryRefreshToken , PRT, DeviceId=d4819c02-5511-4a90-8111-223344556677, IrRemediation=Disable/delete rogue DeviceId + Revoke-MgUserSignInSession so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).

steps.detectionAndEvidence: Documented in Network Event 200 (recording LogCategory=Entra ID SignInLogs, IncomingTokenType=primaryRefreshToken , PRT, DeviceId=d4819c02-5511-4a90-8111-223344556677, IrRemediation=Disable/delete rogue DeviceId + Revoke-MgUserSignInSession under T1550.001): During Entra ID incident response, always audit all devices registered to the compromised user; resetting a user password without disabling rogue registered devices allows a stolen PRT + device key to mint new tokens.
